rule.description: Reports declarations that scatter a cohesive built-in traversal policy group (how the Date, Error and RegExp built-in families are treated while a type is deeply rewritten) into loose, separately declared and separately forwarded boolean boundaries instead of one bundled abstraction.

checks.description: Detect type-alias declarations that declare two or more boolean-typed built-in policy members and re-pass those members one at a time as separate type arguments across recursive boundaries, with no bundled abstraction carrying the group.
checks.detected_relation: built-in traversal policy values (Date/Error/RegExp handling) repeatedly passed together as separate standalone boundaries
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The same cohesive policy group travels member-by-member across recursive production boundaries with no bundled abstraction: every recursion site of every deep rewriter must spell out all members, and every consumer that owns a built-in decision must re-declare the whole machine.

matches.evidence: scattered built-in traversal policy group [DatePolicy, ErrorPolicy, RegexpPolicy] declared as 3 loose boundaries on DeepPartialBuiltin (TSTypeAliasDeclaration); members individually govern traversal branches: DatePolicy->Date, ErrorPolicy->Error, RegexpPolicy->RegExp

excluded: lib/paths/index.ts (PathsOptions: recursion depth and array-index accessor flags belong to a different options domain and are not passed together with any built-in family decision)
lib/deep-mark-optional/index.ts, lib/deep-mark-required/index.ts, lib/mark-* (key-set markers make no built-in traversal decision)
lib/deep-modify.ts (only defines allowed structural filter shapes)
lib/create-type-options/index.ts (generic record-merge helper; itself parameterized by one options record rather than loose per-member boundaries)
lib/functions/is-exact/index.ts (its BooleanXor<T, U> switches are boolean algebra over unconstrained generic values, not declared boolean policy members)
all lib/**/*.test.ts, *.display.ts helpers, and test-types.ts / test-const.ts / ts-version.ts (non-production sources are out of the rule's scan scope)
